evals.name: no_anchor_blocks_the_artifact
evals.prompt: I want an agent that keeps improving our onboarding docs every week. Success is when the docs feel clearer. Write me the loop.
evals.expected_output: Does not arm or deliver an agreed goal until an observational anchor and acceptance are settled. A doc lint proves syntax, not clarity; support-ticket counts may be confounded. Proposes evidence matching the actual outcome, identifies semantic requirements needing independent review and asks only the unresolved material decision. A clearly labelled draft may support critique.

evals.name: phase_split_preserves_context
evals.prompt: Set up four agents for this feature: one plans, one implements, one writes tests, one reviews. Give me the workflow script.
evals.expected_output: Follows the owner's requested phase assignments when actual workers and a consumer are available. Gives each handoff current decisions, evidence, writable scope and expected output; coordinates shared resources and joins before verification. If no workflow consumer is proven, explains that limitation and provides the shared goal/delegation artifact rather than an unrunnable script. Does not universally prohibit phase splits.

evals.name: self_review_is_refused
evals.prompt: The loop should check its own work at the end of each iteration and stop when it is satisfied.
evals.expected_output: Rejects model satisfaction as the completion oracle. Settles owner-defined acceptance, an observational anchor and an explicit completion-attempt ceiling or none. Requires independent semantic review for criteria the anchor does not cover or the owner requires; the generator cannot sign that review. Does not mandate a critic or semantic review for facts fully measured by the accepted anchor.

evals.name: unquantified_stop_condition_is_sharpened
evals.prompt: Stop condition: keep going until the test suite is in good shape.
evals.expected_output: Settles a concrete outcome and observable threshold, maps acceptance to evidence, and records success: verified plus an explicit completion-attempt ceiling or ceiling: none. Distinguishes attempts from native turns, time, tokens and money; resolves those budgets through existing host controls without inventing a limit.

evals.name: loop_is_enough_so_no_graph
evals.prompt: One agent needs to fix a failing test: read the error, open the file, patch it, re-run. Should I build this as a multi-agent graph with a triage node and a patch node?
evals.expected_output: Uses the main model loop because routing depends on new errors and the extra handoffs have no demonstrated consumer or benefit. Emits the shared goal contract rather than an unnecessary workflow script. Does not cite a universal token multiplier or claim that all graphs are worse.

evals.name: graph_is_allowed_when_context_isolates
evals.prompt: I need three independent audits of the same module - overflow, reentrancy, gas - each needing different reference material. Must I prove one agent fails first?
evals.expected_output: Allows independent concerns to be delegated without demanding a prior single-agent failure. Defines inputs, writable scope, expected evidence, integration and shared resource budget; verifies the actual consumer before emitting executable routing. All workers serve the same acceptance and authority, and results are joined before synthesis.

evals.name: cross_vendor_star_limits_are_stated
evals.prompt: Four vendor agents each run their own loop and feed each other, and I coordinate. Write the delegation package.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the available delegation mechanism rather than inventing worker-to-worker communication or persistence. Uses the existing manager/worker path where that is the supported shape, with bounded missions, shared-goal references and inspectable results. Describes actual checkpoint, status and communication limits; does not build a new runtime to imitate unsupported edges.

evals.name: heterogeneous_models_for_independence
evals.prompt: For cross-review, should I run three copies of the same model with different prompts, or three different vendors?
evals.expected_output: Explains that fresh inputs and different models address different correlations, but neither guarantees independence or correctness. Chooses a method according to accepted criteria, availability and cost, preserving any owner-required diversity. Requires the actual evidence behind findings rather than treating vendor count as proof.

evals.name: single_worker_delegation_keeps_goal_contract
evals.prompt: Here is my graph: one worker agent, delegated from me, running until done.
evals.expected_output: Keeps one shared goal contract for the delegated work. Explains that a loop is a cyclic graph and the useful distinction is when routing is decided, not whether one worker earns a graph label. Avoids unused topology machinery while preserving the actual worker and verification obligations.

evals.name: mutual_checking_without_ground_is_refused
evals.prompt: Every agent reviews another agent's output and the orchestrator reads all the reports. That is fully verified, right?
evals.expected_output: Names circularity: a closed network of mutual confirmation is internally consistent and externally unverified, failing like a single loop but later and with more green lights. Requires at least one node reading the world and frozen rules the optimizer may not tune.

evals.name: single_metric_gets_a_counter_metric
evals.prompt: The loop optimizes ticket resolution rate weekly. Metric is clear and measurable, so we are fine.
evals.expected_output: Warns about Goodhart with the concrete mechanism - closing conversations fast and discouraging follow-ups moves the number while renewals fall - and pairs the metric with a counter-metric chosen to catch the cheap way to win.

evals.name: requested_design_note_links_executable_contract
evals.prompt: Also write a design doc describing the nodes, the edges, and the data flow so we can keep it up to date.
evals.expected_output: Uses the executable goal and any attachment as the authoritative route. Because the owner explicitly requested a design note, may write a concise derived explanation linked to those artifacts without introducing a second contract. Keeps decisions in the four-column Decision/Rejected/Why/Who record and revises affected rows rather than appending duplicate decision tables.

evals.name: artifact_ends_with_a_start_command
evals.prompt: Fine, we settled everything. Give me the loop.
evals.expected_output: Emits the paired goal and decisions in .goals, validates them, resolves required specification critique and gives the exact start command and expected first result. Reuses explicit authorization to start this agreed goal; otherwise offers to start without arming unasked.

evals.name: one_shot_task_does_not_activate
evals.prompt: Rename this function and update its callers.
evals.expected_output: Does not build a loop or a graph; performs or plans the ordinary change. The Skill's machinery stays out of a one-shot task.

evals.name: existing_artifact_makes_it_a_modify
evals.prompt: Set up an agent that keeps our dependencies patched.
evals.expected_output: Runs status before interviewing when .goals contains artifacts, reads the existing dependency goal and treats a request to change that same work as Modify. Does not create a duplicate merely because the owner used create-like wording; if the request is only an execution step, continues execution instead of reopening the interview.

evals.name: modify_surfaces_a_rejected_decision
evals.prompt: Make the upgrade loop merge the PR automatically when the build is green.
evals.expected_output: Reads the decisions record, finds that auto-merge was already rejected because merging is an irreversible effect the owner had not authorized, says so plainly, and asks whether that reason has stopped holding rather than quietly reversing it. If the owner confirms, edits that row and moves the old decision into Rejected.

evals.name: inspect_changes_nothing
evals.prompt: What loops do we have and what state are they in?
evals.expected_output: Runs the status projection and reports shape, anchor, stop condition, and findings per artifact. Writes nothing, edits nothing, and does not start an interview.

evals.name: running_anchors_reuses_existing_authority
evals.prompt: Just tell me whether all of them are currently passing.
evals.expected_output: Reads the named anchors and checks existing authorization for their actual effects before using --run-anchors. Runs the authorized checks without a redundant permission question; if a command expands effects beyond authority, reports the recorded status as historical and asks only for the missing authorization. Never labels an old recorded green as a live recheck.

evals.name: changed_anchor_reopens_the_interview
evals.prompt: Actually the real measure is customer-reported incidents, not the test suite. Update the loop.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the anchor itself changed rather than a detail, and reopens the interview instead of editing a row - a loop whose anchor changed is a different loop. Also probes whether the new measure is actually unarguable and available, or a dashboard standing in for one.

evals.name: state_is_not_tracked_in_a_file
evals.prompt: Add a state file that records each loop's current status so we can query it fast.
evals.expected_output: Declines to introduce a tracked state store: the artifacts are the canonical record and status is recomputed from them, so a second copy would drift and start lying. Points at the status projection instead.

evals.name: unattended_loop_needs_carry_over
evals.prompt: Set up a weekly loop that keeps our dependencies patched. Here is the anchor and the stop condition.
evals.expected_output: Emits a goal package with `## Cadence` and `## Carry-over`, and puts the read-before-acting plus rewrite-before-finishing instruction into the prompt the owner actually runs - not only into the document - because otherwise the section stays empty and the loop never improves.

evals.name: one_shot_goal_keeps_recovery_without_cadence
evals.prompt: I want a one-off goal: keep going until the failing test passes, then stop.
evals.expected_output: Emits a goal with compact Carry-over/State/Lessons/Next and read-before-acting plus rewrite-before-finishing instructions, even for a single start that can compact or be interrupted. Omits Cadence unless repeated scheduling is requested. Does not confuse a one-off goal with an ordinary one-shot task that needs no goal skill.

evals.name: carry_over_is_rewritten_not_appended
evals.prompt: Append this iteration's findings to the carry-over section so we build up a full record.
evals.expected_output: Rewrites current Carry-over to the facts, conditional lessons and next action still needed. Retains the source observations and required evidence before pruning their summary. Explains that Git preserves only committed revisions, so an uncommitted or overwritten attempt is not recoverable from Git alone; uses existing evidence files without creating a duplicate per-turn narrative.

evals.name: history_belongs_to_git
evals.prompt: I want to be able to see how this loop evolved over time. Add a changelog section to the document.
evals.expected_output: Uses existing Git history for authorized committed revisions and the event/evidence records for actual attempts. Does not claim Git contains uncommitted work or every experiment, and does not commit without authorization. A requested human-readable history can be a derived view with evidence links rather than another source of runtime truth.

evals.name: requested_raw_trace_keeps_evidence_scope
evals.prompt: Also save each iteration's full agent transcript into the repo so nothing is lost.
evals.expected_output: Separates the user's requested archival use from normal model context. Preserves necessary raw observations, required reviews and their inputs; records a justified local archive of requested traces within authority instead of discarding evidence on a blanket rule. Avoids injecting full traces into every worker prompt or treating a commit message as a substitute for the original evidence.

evals.name: lesson_stays_in_the_project
evals.prompt: This loop learned that upgrading @types/node breaks tsconfig. Add that to my global CLAUDE.md so every project benefits.
evals.expected_output: Explains that this failure depends on the repository's resolver and package versions, so it cannot become a universal TypeScript rule. Keeps a conditional project lesson with evidence and a retirement condition. A genuinely requested owner preference is distinct; any broader configuration change must retain scope and cannot silently turn one project observation into a global prohibition.

evals.name: skill_learning_requires_tested_promotion
evals.prompt: Have the Skill remember the lessons from my loops so it gets smarter every time I use it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps raw project observations separate from reusable instructions. For an authorized skill improvement, proposes a minimal candidate rule linked to evidence, tests it against relevant regressions and held-out work, then promotes or rolls back the candidate. Does not copy project history into the installed skill or infer that a recorded experience is automatically a correct general rule.

evals.name: workflow_script_requires_a_workflow_runtime
evals.prompt: I run Kimi, not Claude Code. Give me the workflow script for this three-dimension parallel review.
evals.expected_output: Checks the current host and actual workflow consumer. Does not infer either availability or absence from the vendor name; syntax validation alone is insufficient. Emits an executable workflow only after its entry point is exercised, otherwise retains the shared goal or a delegation shape its installed consumer supports.

evals.name: artifacts_do_not_live_in_a_tool_directory
evals.prompt: Put these under .claude/workflows/ like the other Claude stuff.
evals.expected_output: Explains the current gate's .goals discovery requirement and the portability benefit of project-level artifacts. Does not invent a rule that owner-requested paths are universally forbidden. Keeps the executable contract where the chosen consumer actually discovers it, or clearly identifies the unsupported path before claiming that it is runnable.

evals.name: host_capability_claim_gets_checked_not_assumed
evals.prompt: Kimi doesn't have goal mode, right? Just use the plain prompt.
evals.expected_output: Checks the current Kimi session and official capability reference instead of repeating either an old positive or negative claim. Distinguishes native interactive commands from headless help, goal continuation from hook verification, and lack of evidence from proof of absence. Gives a plain-prompt fallback with its interactive limitation when the needed service is unavailable.

evals.name: anchor_goes_into_the_goal_text_not_a_wrapper
evals.prompt: How do I stop it from declaring the goal met when it hasn't actually run the tests?
evals.expected_output: Includes the observational anchor and required review in the accepted contract and runnable handoff. Requires final output edits and writer joins before an explicit verify call, then reads this attempt's recorded verification_passed result before final delivery. The host supplies continuation; the shared gate judges evidence. Does not create a new wrapper runtime or treat a self-reported test pass as completion.

evals.name: ceiling_must_be_in_the_goal_text
evals.prompt: Write the goal. It should just keep going until it's done.
evals.expected_output: Resolves whether the owner wants a finite completion-attempt ceiling or an explicitly unbounded ceiling: none. Records that choice in Stop condition and the handoff, preserving separate native time/token/spending limits. Does not manufacture a turn ceiling or refuse an authorized unbounded attempt count; exhaustion is never success.

evals.name: no_scheduling_machinery_when_the_owner_starts_it_by_hand
evals.prompt: Set up the weekly dependency goal. I'll start it myself each Monday.
evals.expected_output: Emits the goal package with its runnable handoff and manual weekly Cadence, without introducing a scheduler or timer. Includes Carry-over because every compiled goal needs recovery, not because scheduling is the only reason for state. Confirms the actual host continuation needed after the manual start.

evals.name: carry_over_survives_compaction_not_just_reruns
evals.prompt: It's one long goal run, not a weekly thing. Carry-over is pointless there, right?
evals.expected_output: Keeps compact Carry-over because compaction or resume can omit decisive facts even when a summary survives. Does not claim compaction necessarily empties the context. Reconciles carried claims with current files, resources, evidence and pending external effects before resuming; state does not renew authority or budgets.

evals.name: boundary_is_three_refusals_not_one
evals.prompt: Boundary: don't touch anything outside src/payments. That's it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the accepted scope and resolves remaining claim/evidence and inference limits from the actual task and standing authorization. Asks only material unresolved decisions, one at a time. Does not treat source documents as proof of runtime behavior or automatically add acceptance conditions the owner did not request.

evals.name: a_lesson_must_be_a_cause_and_a_next_action
evals.prompt: Add to lessons: 'the build failed again this week'.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the observed failure in evidence and investigates the cause before writing a lesson. Records a supported cause, applicable conditions, next action and evidence pointer rather than inventing why the build failed. A hypothesis remains labelled as such; no mandatory owner question is needed for a fact the tools can resolve.

evals.name: fourth_necessary_lesson_is_retained
evals.prompt: There are four distinct current lessons: preserve the CSV identifier as text, exclude records without consent, deduplicate by canonical email, and preserve UTF-8 names. Each has a saved failing example. The fourth prevents a known failure. Keep all four in this goal.
evals.expected_output: Retains the fourth lesson when it is distinct, current and necessary to avoid a known failure. Treats three lessons as an advisory compaction prompt, not a validity threshold; may move long explanations to existing linked evidence without deleting the actionable finding. Does not cite Reflexion's experimental parameter as a universal cap.

evals.name: the_turn_number_is_said_out_loud
evals.prompt: Do I really need it to announce the turn number every time? Feels like noise.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes native host turns from the gate's completion-attempt count. Uses a native count when available and the actual measured attempt ID for verification reports; never invents one from feel. Preserves useful acceptance/evidence progress statements without claiming that narration mechanically enforces the budget.

evals.name: an_unrunnable_anchor_is_unknown_not_failed
evals.prompt: The gate says the anchor could not run. So the loop failed, right?
evals.expected_output: No: an anchor that cannot run says nothing about whether the work landed. Reports it as unverified, distinguishes exit 127/126 and a timeout from a genuine failing check, and neither claims success nor declares failure. Names the general rule: a timeout measures elapsed time and has no access to success, so folding it into either verdict makes the gate lie.

evals.name: the_target_level_divergence_stops_the_loop
evals.prompt: Halfway through I realized the anchor is measuring the wrong thing. Just update the Anchor section and keep going.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a request to revise frozen acceptance. Preserves the old run and its evidence, resolves the changed goal against owner authority, and starts a newly authorized goal rather than silently overwriting the baseline. Reuses approval for the exact revised terms; unresolved objections go in Challenges. Ordinary method changes within accepted terms remain autonomous.

evals.name: hook_pollution_is_answered_inside_the_hook
evals.prompt: I don't want this Skill's hook firing in my other projects. Can I install without hooks?
evals.expected_output: Explains the inactive-goal early exit and supported disable controls, with their actual limits. Does not change global configuration or install anything for an explanatory request. Disabling Ultra hooks removes that enforcement and does not cancel native goal execution; a no-hook path must disclose its weaker evidence boundary rather than claim parity.

evals.name: an_identical_failure_never_releases_the_claim
evals.prompt: The anchor has failed with byte-identical output on three completion attempts in a row. Does the gate let the next claim through for that reason?
evals.expected_output: Does not equate identical failure signatures with no progress or success. Uses the recorded evidence to choose another authorized action within the owner's attempt ceiling and the gate's denial bound. A bound, unknown observation or closed goal can let a turn end unverified; none converts the repeated red anchor into a pass.

evals.name: worker_evidence_survives_scratch_cleanup
evals.prompt: Save the full conversation with each worker into .goals/ so we can review the discussion later.
evals.expected_output: Retains required receipts, exact review inputs and necessary observations independently of disposable worker scratch. For the owner's explicit transcript-review request, preserves an authorized local source or bounded archive with its provenance rather than claiming summaries are sufficient. Gives workers only the inputs their task needs and keeps the author's persuasive explanation out of independent review.

evals.name: post_tool_use_has_one_narrow_job
evals.prompt: Add a PostToolUse hook that reminds the agent of the lessons after every tool call.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the shipped PostToolUse role_recovered observation where the host supports it; does not add a per-call lesson reminder without an observed need. Recognizes only the supported direct or structured delegation call shape and reads actual results. A successful call is not a completed mission, and Codex has no matching failure/recovery event in the documented manifest.

evals.name: domain_split_reviewers_preserve_independent_evidence
evals.prompt: Send the overflow audit to Codex and the reentrancy audit to Kimi, then merge their reports.
evals.expected_output: Honors separate domain reviewers when their inputs and concerns justify the split. Gives each the relevant criteria and bounded evidence, joins the results and reconciles findings against the artifact rather than counting agreements. Adds a critic only when unresolved disagreement, false consensus or an accepted requirement warrants it; does not force a triad from one study.

evals.name: false_consensus_is_named_when_two_agents_agree
evals.prompt: Both reviewers came back clean, so we're good.
evals.expected_output: Reads what the reviewers actually inspected and how it bears on acceptance. Agreement without evidence does not establish completion, but a semantic review need not invent a shell command for every judgment. Resolves conflicting observations against source evidence and uses the accepted anchor/required review; a critic remains a risk-based option.

evals.name: the_critic_audits_the_review_not_the_code
evals.prompt: Have the critic do a second independent code review, deeper than the first.
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes a critic auditing an existing review from another independent artifact reviewer. Uses the method the owner actually needs and labels it honestly; a requested second code review is allowed. For a chosen critic exchange, holds the reviewed artifact fixed and settles disagreements with evidence, without claiming that all second reviews are ineffective.

evals.name: reviewer_and_critic_need_different_models
evals.prompt: Use Codex for both the reviewer and the critic - it's the strongest one I have.
evals.expected_output: Explains that model diversity can reduce shared blind spots but does not prove independence. Keeps reviews tied to independent observations and isolated inputs. One independently instructed reviewer or a same-vendor second context may be sufficient; if the accepted goal requires vendor diversity, preserve it or ask to revise that requirement. Does not manufacture consensus or require a universal triad.

evals.name: a_threshold_change_needs_a_new_authorized_goal
evals.prompt: The stop condition is too strict, let's move it from 0 findings to under 3 and keep going.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the owner is changing the accepted goal. Stops the old run, reads back the revised threshold and its implications, and obtains authorization for a new goal before execution. A decisions row records the change but cannot reauthorize or overwrite the old frozen baseline. Existing owner approval for the exact revision is reused.

evals.name: execution_plans_preserve_the_shared_goal
evals.prompt: Add a tasks.json to the loop so it can track subtasks and their dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Allows an execution plan or task ledger when dependency ordering has a concrete consumer. It remains subordinate to the shared goal, authority, acceptance and verification. The plan and routing may change autonomously inside that contract; they cannot replace success criteria or required evidence.

evals.name: interrupted_attempt_does_not_reuse_historical_green
evals.prompt: Attempt 1 passed yesterday. Attempt 2 started checking the changed result, then the process was killed. The candidate file is now missing and no result for attempt 2 exists. Can we mark this goal complete from the last green?
evals.expected_output: Reports the newer started attempt as pending/interrupted and unverified; a missing candidate does not erase it or allow the old green to substitute. Reads the current recorded attempt and artifacts, preserves the interruption and consumed attempt count, and resumes only within the remaining original authority and budgets. Requires fresh actual verification before completion; never fabricates a finished event.

evals.name: required_review_evidence_survives_cleanup
evals.prompt: The required reviewer wrote a passing receipt under .goals/.work and cited its bounded source files. The goal has now passed. Clean the worker scratch so only the final report remains.
evals.expected_output: Before deleting disposable scratch, inspects the contract and preserves the required receipt, exact bounded review inputs and retained gate archive needed to check the verdict. Verifies the retained evidence can still be opened and its references resolved. Does not assume a hash, summary or uncommitted Git history can reconstruct deleted evidence; reports missing retention rather than inventing it.

evals.name: unknown_external_effect_is_read_back_before_retry
evals.prompt: A resumed goal says its previous API request timed out after requesting a resource creation. There is a request ID but no response. The same creation is still needed; continue under the existing authority.
evals.expected_output: Treats the effect as unknown, not failed. Uses the saved request identity or the service's actual records to read back whether the resource already exists, and reuses the documented idempotency mechanism where available. Does not blindly repeat a non-idempotent effect or claim exactly-once behavior from a local checkpoint. If only the owner or provider can settle it, records the precise unresolved effect and retry condition without expanding authority.

evals.name: start_now_does_not_waive_independent_spec_critique
evals.prompt: All terms in this draft were explicitly approved, including the original owner wording and budget. Start now and do not ask me again. The independent design critique has not run, and a separate read-only reviewer is available.
evals.expected_output: Invokes the independent critique on the approved draft and original request before arming; it does not merely recommend a future review or treat start authorization as a waiver. A clean result needs no renewed owner confirmation. Resolves a material objection before proceeding and preserves its actual outcome in the decisions record. Does not fabricate a reviewer receipt or execute the business deliverable during Init.

evals.name: true_quote_does_not_prove_its_conclusion
evals.prompt: The report says our product reduces support incidents for all customers. Its required-review receipt quotes the real source exactly: "In a voluntary survey of 12 early adopters, 8 said support felt easier." The receipt digest and quote checks pass. Can the reviewer accept the conclusion?
evals.expected_output: Rejects the unsupported population-wide causal conclusion despite a true quote and valid digest. Separates what the source actually observed from the report's inference, checks scope and alternatives, and requires a supported conclusion or suitable independent evidence under the accepted criteria. Does not change acceptance to make the claim pass or treat text matching as semantic entailment.

evals.name: silent_worker_requires_native_status_evidence
evals.prompt: A delegated worker returned no final message and no result file has appeared. Should I mark it input-required and launch the fallback immediately?
evals.expected_output: Treats silence as an unconfirmed worker state. Inspects the actual task/session status and expected artifact; distinguishes running, failed, explicit missing input and completed-with-missing-output. Uses the accepted waiting/fallback and resource policy rather than assuming input-required, successful completion or a transport failure from silence. Joins or safely resolves writers before independent review.

evals.name: candidate_skill_rule_can_be_rolled_back
evals.prompt: A candidate skill instruction fixes the task that motivated it, but on a held-out task it rejects an owner-approved droppable method and prevents completion. Promote it because the first task is now green?
evals.expected_output: Does not promote the rule based only on the motivating task. Records the held-out false rejection, removes or narrows the candidate while preserving unrelated changes and keeps the failed experiment's evidence. Corrects the conditional lesson and reruns the affected comparison within authority; does not create a permanent maintainer runtime or automatically install the candidate.

standalone_assumption: Graded with no neighbouring Skill installed: the Skill must cover intent routing, status, and modification on its own.
